SMTO-MEM-0016 — SMTO can't sign in to the model that makes text searchable

GUID: 0e083882-8fa6-5c09-a80e-e1ba42b42c4a
Slug: knowledge-embedding-credentials-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Knowledge uses an embeddings model to turn your documents and memories into searchable data. Its saved connection is missing its key or no longer matches the assigned model, so this indexing or search couldn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and expand Embeddings. Choose the instance and select Assign Embeddings, or enter the external API key again if it shows API key missing. Assigning again saves a fresh connection and key that match the current embeddings model.
  2. If Knowledge's Document settings use Remote text endpoint, check that the Parameter Store entry named in Credential parameter key has an api_key value. For a remote service, SMTO reads the key from that Parameter Store entry, and it was missing or empty.
  3. In Knowledge › Document settings, select Apply Embeddings and rebuild if needed. This makes Knowledge use the connection you just assigned.
  4. Select Retry failed jobs in Knowledge, or Manage › Reindex on the affected document. Once the connection works, the stopped indexing can run again safely.

What success looks like

  • Documents show Ready to search, and Test retrieval returns passages.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete your documents or the Memory index; their search data can be rebuilt once the connection works.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Embedding encode failed with embedding_credentials_unavailable: the managed Embeddings binding is missing or no longer matches the assigned instance, encoder, model or endpoint, or the remote provider's credential_key has no api_key in the Parameter Store.

What this means

  • The saved embedding connection does not currently provide the credentials needed to use it. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported embedding_credentials_unavailable. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • An explicit embedding test succeeds with the selected connection.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • For provider=managed, reassign Embeddings in Settings, Model routing so the binding matches the profile's managed instance, encoder and model, then use Apply Embeddings in Knowledge settings. For provider=http, store an api_key field in the Parameter Store entry named by credential_key. Then retry failed jobs.
  • Ask an administrator to open model settings and reconnect the embedding provider, then check Knowledge again.

Retry and execution caution

  • An explicit embedding test succeeds with the selected connection.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicit embedding test succeeds with the selected connection.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
